The quantity of spent catalysts discarded from the water gas shift unit is always higher than that of the fresh catalyst amount loaded in the reactor because of the formation of coke, sulfur (if present in feed), and the other metal deposits on the catalysts during the entire process. For example, spent catalysts from WGS units typically contain carbon along with some oil and oxides initially present in the catalyst. The spent catalyst comes under the category of hazardous industrial waste. Therefore, it cannot be disposed of for landfilling (the landfill does not remove or destroy any hazardous materials if risks are not adequately managed, and it may pose long-term health and environmental hazards and gets affected by future regulatory changes). Spent catalyst management requires specialized expertise, including regeneration, rejuvenation, metal recovery, and reuse. Many spent catalysts contain high concentrations of metals or other materials that are economically worth recovering. It has been envisaged that third-party vendors with expertise will be contacted for spent catalyst management. The vendor will take care of spent catalysts. For these activities, suitable cost provision has been made in project cost. However, the vendor should prepare safety documentation for the spent catalyst management. The document should contain the information necessary to determine how the spent catalyst can be safely and correctly handled, classified, packaged, labelled, stored, transported, and treated/processed. Some features need to be verified before the disposal of the spent catalyst. It will include the following: • Composition and properties of the original catalyst • Treatment of spent catalyst after discharge to ensure that it is obtained in the best state for further handling or processing • If the catalyst has been contaminated in use • The expected chemical and physical characteristics of the spent catalyst • If the spent catalyst has any potentially hazardous properties • The appropriate procedure for spent catalyst classification, with proper packaging, labeling, storing, transportation, and discharge mechanism.
